Area Rug Buying Guide: Size, Style, & Tips for Every Room

By Casey FinnPosted on October 20, 2025
Listen to audio version of this article
0:00 / 0:00 Instaread
Sponsored by

Choosing the right rug for your home can feel overwhelming. In this guide, I break down everything you need to know about buying a rug before you hit “Add to Cart.”

I get it, buying a rug can feel like a big decision. They’re not cheap; they cover a ton of real estate in a room, and the wrong choice can throw the whole space off.

The upside: a rug is also an easy way to make a room cozy, and this guide covers each choice so you can pick with confidence.

Choosing a Rug: What to Consider First

A rug can be a quiet backdrop, like the large seagrass rug, or the star, like the olive and charcoal 9×12 rug.

Weigh function first: foot traffic, spills, kids on the floor, and whether your flooring needs a non-slip pad.

Picture everyday use before falling for a color or pattern.

Rug Materials: What to Consider

  • Wool rugs: stain-resistant, cozy and long-lasting; the top pick.
  • Natural fiber rugs (jute, sisal, seagrass): tough and cheap, but scratchy (full guide).
  • Cotton flatweaves: light and inexpensive, though short-lived.
  • Synthetic rugs (polypropylene, nylon): affordable and kid- and pet-friendly.
  • Vintage rugs: pricier but durable, as in Rory’s bedroom.
Shopping Tip:

Test an unfamiliar material with a sample or matching doormat first.

How to Buy Rugs Online

Most of these rugs were bought online, where comparing styles, waiting for sales and returning are easy.

Done right, it can beat a store on price and ease:

  • Read reviews carefully. Buyer photos show true color.
  • Check return policies. Skip costly returns.
  • Order a sample. See texture at home.
  • Compare prices across retailers. Google Lens helps (more tips).

Best Places to Buy Rugs

The go-to shops, after trying many:

  • RugsUSA: wait for sales, up to 70% off.
  • Lulu & Georgia: on-trend patterns.
  • Loloi: good prices, often via Amazon.
  • Wayfair: huge variety.
  • West Elm: see rugs in person.
  • Anthropologie: whimsical and pricey.
  • Pottery Barn: timeless neutrals.
  • HomeGoods: bargains, like my mom’s bedroom rug.
Shopping Tip:

Search a rug’s name or model number to find it cheaper elsewhere.

Vintage Rugs: Why They’re Worth It

True vintage rugs are hand-knotted wool built to last and one of a kind, which is why vintage Turkish pieces fill the nursery, guest bath and kitchen.

For the kitchen, a Serapi runner from eBay (2.5 by 12 feet) brought the room to life.

My Favorite Vintage Rug Shops

Beyond Etsy and eBay, try:

  • Canary Lane
  • ESale Rugs
  • Loom House
  • New England Loom
  • Revival Rugs
  • Violet Vintage Rugs
  • Vintage Rug Shop
  • Zuma Imports
  • eCarpet Gallery

Unique pieces sell fast, so check often and search terms like Turkish or Oushak.

Buying Tip:

A small vintage runner is an affordable first step.

Outdoor Rugs

Outdoor rugs make a patio feel like a room. Given Chicago weather, cheap ones lasting a season or two make sense, with a power wash when dirty, and they invite bold pattern.

Rug Size Guide: Finding the Right Rug Size

The most common mistake is a rug that’s too small. Quick rules follow (full size guide).

  • Living Room: front legs on the rug; 8×10 or 9×12.
  • Dining Room: 24″ past the table all around.
  • Bedroom: 18–24″ per side; 8×10 queen, 9×12 king.
  • Hallways/Kitchens: durable natural-fiber runners.
Design Tip:

When unsure, go bigger.

Quick Rug FAQ

Can I layer rugs (even over carpet)?

Yes, to add color and zones; carpet tape keeps it put.

Do I need a rug pad?
Yes, on hard floors. Try felt and rubber, trimmed with electric scissors.

How thick should a rug pad be?
About 1/4″ for thin rugs; mind door clearance.

How do you clean rugs?
Vacuum, spot clean, use the Little Green, and steam clean yearly.

Can I donate my old rug?
Yes if clean; otherwise recycle it.

Should you put a rug under a dining table?
Only low pile, and not with small kids.

How do you do multiple rugs in the same room?
Mix two pattern types, like jute with an organic design.

How do you get the edges of the rug to lie flat?
Weigh corners, add rug tape, or reverse-roll.

How long should a rug last?
Good wool, for generations.

What’s your favorite kid-friendly rug?
The living room rug; it hides everything.

Is Ruggable worth it? Casey’s mom likes her washable one.

Do you prefer carpet or rug for a bedroom? A rug on hardwood.

Can a rug help distract from other busy elements in a space? Yes; a neutral one can calm a room (easy updates).
